text: TEVRA provides novel aggregate-level inter-clonal CDR3 convergence metric computed using nhood_cdr3_convergence(). reports similarity CDR3 amino acid sequences distinct clonotypes, within aggregate. aggregate high CDR3 convergence represents one clonotypes converging onto similar CDR3 sequence, therefore likely respond epitope. Alternatively, aggregate low CDR3 convergence suggests clonotypes respond multiple antigens multiple epitopes antigen dissimilar sequences. function computes heavy light chain CDR3 sequences chain = “”. details specifically metric computed, refer section end vignette. key metrics : receptor_type: TCRs, similarity scores computed unique CDR3 sequence represent unique clones. BCRs, somatic hypermutation enables CDR3 sequences clone different sequences. Hence, representative centroid first selected per clone CDR3 sequence similar CDR3 sequences clone. min_n_contigs: minimum number contigs required per aggregate. Must exceed min_clones. min_clones: minimum number clones required per aggregate. substitution_weighting: CDR3 sequences can differ either insertions, deletions substitutions. insertions deletions incur cost 1. Using Levenshtein distances, substitutions also incur cost 1. Using blosum-weighted distances, cost substitutions weighted according physicochemical significance substitution (see end vignette details). custom substitution matrix can also supplied unique substitution weightings, ranging -1 (costly substitution) 0 (least costly substitution). summary_metric: inter-clonal convergence scores summarised per aggregate either globally providing mean median score locally. Local convergence scores report mean distance CDR3 sequence \(k\) nearest neighbours, averaged per aggregate (see end vignette details). downsample: TRUE (default), matrices clonal convergence scores downsampled median clonal count n_boots iterations control variation clone number across aggregates. investigate raw convergence matrices without neighbourhood-level summarisation, run nhood_cdr3_convergence_matrices(), can plotted heatmap. title: Test Leiden clustering resolutions on a nearest-neighbour graph — test_resolution
text: function build nearest-neighbour graph . graph must computed stored metadata(sce)$graphs calling function. Two workflows supported: 1. scratch scran: 2. existing Seurat object: value passed graph.name must match key used storing graph metadata(sce)$graphs.
code: library(scran)  # Build a shared nearest-neighbour graph on the PCA embedding g <- scran::buildSNNGraph(sce, use.dimred = "PCA", k = 20)  # Store it under the name this function will look for metadata(sce)$graphs[["RNA_snn"]] <- g library(Seurat)  # Convert to SCE first sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(seurat_obj)  # Extract the adjacency matrix from the Seurat object, convert to igraph, # and store in the SCE metadata g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(   seurat_obj@graphs[["RNA_snn"]],   mode     = "max",   weighted = TRUE ) metadata(sce)$graphs[["RNA_snn"]] <- g
